source: Ismayilzada et al. (2026) CresOWLve: Benchmarking Creative Problem-Solving Over Real-World Knowledge (COLM 2026)
finding: New 2026 benchmark of expert-written insight-style puzzles (What? Where? When?) tested on 2026 frontier models. Thinking models beat non-thinking ones, and models do worse on creative items than matched factual items. Gap 3: 2026 models still fail on this item type.
numbers: 2,061 creative items (EN and RU). Non-thinking models all under 30% accuracy. Creative vs factual drop 6.08% (Gemini-3.1-Pro high) to 17.21% (Mistral-Large-3) on EN, bootstrap 1000 iterations, difficulty balanced. Even the best models lose over 20 points from Very Simple to Very Hard.
quote: models can often retrieve the relevant knowledge, they struggle to form the non-obvious creative connections
limits: Items are decades old and public; the authors admit contamination. Factual subset is only 352 items. No human run (items were solved once by expert teams).
agent_relevance: Test the scaffold on a 2026 model here. The failure is the link between facts, not recall, so a retrieval add-on will not help; a reframe or connection step might.

source: Ismayilzada et al. (2026) CresOWLve: Benchmarking Creative Problem-Solving Over Real-World Knowledge (COLM 2026) - effort scaling
finding: More thinking effort raises accuracy on creative items within one model, also for open models where the contamination asymmetry is absent. Relevant to the equal-token question (gap 1).
numbers: GPT-5.4 nearly doubles from no thinking to medium effort: 9.4% to 17.8% (EN), 15.4% to 26.9% (RU). Thinking advantage also holds for DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5, Qwen3.5-397B.
limits: Single run per setting; effort levels are not matched on token count across models; no equal-token comparison against a scaffold.
agent_relevance: Baseline for our scaffold: compare against the same model at higher effort, not against a no-thinking model.

source: Ismayilzada et al. (2026) CresOWLve: Benchmarking Creative Problem-Solving Over Real-World Knowledge (COLM 2026) - contamination test
finding: Direct contamination test on an insight-style set. Gemini-3.1-Pro scored far higher on the Russian text than on the English translation, and picked the true item among perturbed copies far above chance. So gap 3 is partly closed: contamination is real for old public puzzle sets and can inflate scores.
numbers: 580 items answered right in Russian but not English. Quiz with the correct item in a non-preferred slot: 72%, 73%, 74% over 3 runs (mean 73%) vs 25% chance. Closed thinking models up to +15 pts (LLM judge) and +18 pts (exact match) higher on RU than EN.
limits: Method follows Golchin and Surdeanu (2025); it shows exposure, not that answers were memorised. One model tested this way.
agent_relevance: Never report scaffold gains on old public insight sets alone. Use items written after the model cutoff.

source: Ismayilzada et al. (2026) CresOWLve: Benchmarking Creative Problem-Solving Over Real-World Knowledge (COLM 2026) - error analysis
finding: Authors hand-labelled why frontier thinking models fail. Missing creative connection and clue misinterpretation dominate; hallucination and wrong-reference errors (retrieval failure) are rare. Anchoring is a separate, smaller class.
numbers: 1,087 error examples from GPT-5.4 (medium); 150 sampled and labelled by three authors. Category shares are given per model with Wilson 95% CI half-widths of about 1 to 4 points. The table layout was garbled in text extraction, so per-column values are not recorded here.
limits: Three annotators on 150 cases; categories chosen by the authors; per-column numbers not verified.
agent_relevance: Supports a connection-forcing or clue-recheck operator over a knowledge-fetch operator.

source: Nieuwenstein et al. (2015) On making the right choice: a meta-analysis and large-scale replication attempt of the unconscious thought advantage (JDM 10(1):1-17)
finding: Closes the numbers part of gap 6. The meta-analysis of the 'distraction beats deliberation' claim shows a small raw effect that vanishes after bias correction.
numbers: k = 61 effect sizes (81 multi-attribute studies found). Random-effects g = 0.15, 95% CI [0.03, 0.26], p = .01. Asymmetry test Z = 2.11, p = .04. Trim-and-fill g = 0.018, CI [-0.10, 0.14], p = .77. Non-composite sensitivity: g = 0.14, after trim-and-fill g = -0.01.
quote: the overall effect size of the UTA turned non-significant
limits: About multi-attribute decision tasks, not insight problems. No subgroup analysis. Read from the journal HTML page via a fetch tool (the PDF would not download).
agent_relevance: Do not cite this as a failure of incubation on insight. It only weakens the unconscious-thought mechanism (see K02).

finding: Within-subject replication built to favour the effect found none.
numbers: N = 399 (130 men, 269 women; 24 non-native speakers excluded from 423). Accuracy: deliberation 58.2%, distraction 61.9%; mode of thought Wald chi2 = 1.09, p = .30; mode x gender chi2 = .02, p = .90. First-condition between-subjects: 55.61% (N=196) vs 55.17% (N=203). Bayes factor 7.83 for the null.
limits: Choice task with a word-search distractor; says nothing about insight tasks.

source: Nieuwenstein et al. (2015) task scope check
finding: The paper uses no insight tasks. So the second half of gap 6 stays open: I found no large or many-labs-style failed replication of incubation on insight problems since 2015 in the sources I could reach. Search tools were exhausted, so this is a source not found, not proof of absence.
numbers: 0 insight tasks in the paper. Sio and Ormerod 2009 (a12) remains the only insight-relevant meta-analysis in our files (d=0.29).
limits: Literature search for post-2015 insight-incubation replications was not possible: web search budget exhausted, arXiv API and Semantic Scholar rate-limited.
agent_relevance: Treat the K01 effect (d about 0.2 to 0.3) as pre-2015 data only.

source: Huang et al. (2024) Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet (ICLR 2024)
finding: Without an outside signal, asking the model to review and fix its own answer lowers accuracy. Earlier gains came from using the correct label to decide when to stop. Relevant to gap 1: an ungated forced reconsideration can hurt.
numbers: GPT-4 intrinsic self-correction: GSM8K 95.5 to 91.5 (round 1) to 89.0 (round 2); CommonSenseQA 82.0 to 79.5 to 80.0; HotpotQA 49 to 49 to 43. GPT-3.5: GSM8K 75.9 to 75.1 to 74.7; CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1 to 41.8; HotpotQA 26 to 25 to 25. GPT-3.5 kept its first answer 74.7% of the time on GSM8K; changes were more often correct-to-wrong than wrong-to-correct.
quote: The fundamental issue is that LLMs cannot properly judge the correctness of their reasoning
limits: 2023-era GPT-3.5, GPT-4 and Llama-2, not reasoning models; math and QA, not insight items.
agent_relevance: Any reconsideration step needs an external or check-based gate (code run, constraint check), not self-judgement. Supports commit-by-check (gap 2).

source: Ghosal et al. (2025) Does Thinking More Always Help? Mirage of Test-Time Scaling in Reasoning Models
finding: Appending 'Wait' to extend one reasoning trace helps at first and then hurts, because output variance grows. Spending the same tokens on independent samples with majority vote does better. This is a direct equal-token comparison of continue-the-attempt versus fresh samples, the closest thing to gap 5 found.
numbers: Same budget: parallel thinking up to 22% higher accuracy than sequential (abstract says 20%). DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B on GSM8K: 'Wait' up to 16,000 tokens gives -11.8% vs standard thinking (385 tokens); parallel at 16,000 gives +10.1%.
limits: Math (GSM8K, MATH-500, AIME 2024), distilled models; majority vote needs a checkable single answer. Not tested on insight items and not a test of a reset-after-impasse operator.
agent_relevance: Prefer fresh independent samples over a longer single chain when stuck. Partial answer to gap 5: resampling beats continuing, on math, at equal tokens.

source: Zhang et al. (2025) Reasoning Models Know When They're Right: Probing Hidden States for Self-Verification
finding: A probe on hidden states predicts whether an intermediate answer is right, and is well calibrated, while the model's own text does not use this. Relevant to gap 8 (trigger choice) and gap 9 (calibration): an internal signal can be calibrated even when verbal checks are not.
numbers: In-distribution ROC-AUC above 0.7 on all datasets, ECE below 0.1; R1-Distill-Qwen-32B over 0.9 ROC-AUC on AIME. Probe-gated early exit cut inference tokens by up to 24% without losing accuracy.
limits: Needs hidden-state access (not available through a normal API). Math and logic tasks; probes trained per dataset, weaker out of distribution.
agent_relevance: An API agent only has text-level triggers. Sample disagreement is the closest outside proxy for this internal signal.

source: Liu et al. (2025) Understanding R1-Zero-Like Training: A Critical Perspective (COLM 2025)
finding: The 'aha moment' self-reflection already appears in the base model DeepSeek-V3-Base, and in R1-Zero more self-reflection does not go with higher accuracy. Supports d'Aliberti: spontaneous aha text is not a sign of restructuring (gap 9).
numbers: 500 MATH questions with the R1 template. Self-reflection counts are higher in R1-Zero than in the base, but 'not positively correlated with higher accuracy'. The base model produces keywords such as 'Aha' and 'wait'.
quote: these behaviors are not positively correlated with higher accuracy
limits: Keyword-based counting of self-reflection, math only; detailed numbers are in the paper's Sec. F, which I did not read.
agent_relevance: Do not use the presence of 'aha' or 'wait' in a trace as a sign that an impasse was solved.

source: Huang et al. (2024) LatEval: An Interactive LLMs Evaluation Benchmark with Incomplete Information from Lateral Thinking Puzzles (LREC-COLING)
finding: Controlled clue-amount test on lateral puzzles: 0%, 50% or 100% of the clues given up front. Strong models get closer to the truth as clues rise; a weak model (Baichuan-chat-13B) cannot even with all clues. This is a controlled hint-quantity manipulation, unlike the Sadeghi log (gap 10), but it varies clue amount, not short vs long hints.
numbers: Interactive puzzles, max 20 turns. Answer consistency, GPT-4 host (first table row read): GPT-4 27.5 (EN) and 25.7 (ZH); GPT-3.5 23.9 and 12.6; Claude 19.6 (EN). Clue effect is shown in a ROUGE-L figure only; no numeric table read.
limits: Figure-only data for the clue manipulation; 2023 models; ROUGE-L is a weak score; no variation of hint length or specificity. Table column mapping read from garbled text.
agent_relevance: Gap 10 stays open for short versus long. Clue amount helps strong models, so hints must be usable by the solver.

source: Lee et al. (2025) Puzzled by Puzzles: When Vision-Language Models Can't Take a Hint
finding: 432 hand-made rebus puzzles (a visual insight type). Retry after being told 'that was incorrect' gives gains that plateau; the gap between 1 and 5 attempts is large even for weak models. Relevant to gaps 1 and 5 because the feedback is external (told wrong), not self-detected.
numbers: Naive/LLM-judged accuracy: GPT-5 60.42/69.44; o3 54.56/54.60; o4-mini 48.16/55.62; gemini-2.5-pro 39.99/47.27; gpt-4o 18.75/26.52; claude-3.7-sonnet 10.20/16.31. Humans: non-expert 16.4-37.23 / 21.86-44.71; expert 76.4 / 80.80. Replacing the image with a caption hurt reasoning models most.
limits: Short paper; retry curve read from text, not a table; feedback is external, which a real agent lacks; puzzles are public web items (contamination not tested).
agent_relevance: Retry with a verified-wrong signal is worth using. A scaffold that can verify a candidate (gap 2) can supply that signal itself.

source: Liu, Karimnazarov and White (2025) Trapped by Expectations: Functional Fixedness in LLM-Enabled Chat Search
finding: Not a test of LLM fixation. It is a human study of how users fixate on how they use ChatGPT. Recorded to rule it out as evidence for gap 4 or gap 7.
numbers: 450 crowd participants, six decision-making tasks; users whose expectations were unmet wrote more detailed, more varied prompts.
limits: Humans using an LLM, not LLM insight; no accuracy outcome.
agent_relevance: Not usable for the agent design. Do not cite for LLM functional fixedness.

source: Gap-search negative result: context reset after impasse (gap 5)
finding: No paper in reach tests 'drop the failed attempt, then sample fresh' as a named operator on insight items. The nearest evidence is d09 (parallel samples beat extended single chains at equal tokens, math) and d08 (self-review without a signal lowers accuracy).
numbers: arXiv title searches for restart, overthinking and fixation returned HTTP 429, so coverage is incomplete.
limits: Absence-of-evidence line. opened is false because no page was read for this line.
agent_relevance: Run our own ablation: continue vs reset-and-resample vs reset-with-failure-summary at equal tokens.

source: Gap-search negative result: externalised state and hints (gaps 7, 10)
finding: No controlled LLM test of 'manipulate external objects or write code' on insight items (the Henok 43% vs 6% analogue) and no controlled short-versus-long hint ablation were found. Closest: d12 (clue amount) and the earlier MacGyver result (c16-c18).
limits: Absence-of-evidence line; search budget was exhausted.
agent_relevance: Both are open and testable in our harness.
